bug_semantics: nltk.internals.java() accepts a per-call `options` parameter (keyword-only, added 2026-07-04) that is spliced directly into the JVM command line: `cmd = [_java_bin] + java_options + cmd`, with `_validate_java_options()` applied only to the GLOBAL options set via config_java(), never to the per-call list. Every Stanford/CoreNLP wrapper (StanfordTagger, StanfordSegmenter, CoreNLPParser/CoreNLPServer) passes user-influenced java_options through this parameter, so an attacker controlling wrapper options can inject arbitrary JVM launcher switches — -agentpath/-javaagent (native/bytecode agent = arbitrary code execution), @argfile (expanded by the Java launcher before other processing, smuggling blocked flags), -XX:OnError/-XX:OnOutOfMemoryError (JVM-executed shell commands) — achieving code execution under the NLTK process' privileges (CWE-88).
flaw_origin: Commit 5ac475d2ab95ea95d2890c745a05e5275137fb98 ("fix(security): isolate Stanford Java options and clean temp files (#3683)", 2026-07-04, author KKfine <74962842+haoami@users.noreply.github.com>, committer GitHub) created the per-call `options` parameter and wired `cmd = [_java_bin] + java_options + cmd` with options taken verbatim from the caller — WITHOUT routing the per-call list through _validate_java_options() (which existed since 9e20c3eee792, 2026-07-01, but guarded only config_java()'s global _java_options). The advisory's named sink — 'per-call options parameter in the java() function' — is born here: before this commit, wrapper options went through config_java() (global mutation) and java() calls used the globally-validated _java_options; no unvalidated direct-splice path existed. The same commit introduced the second defect: relying on an allowlist that blanket-accepts -XX:/-D prefixes (bypassable via -XX:OnError), later replaced by the fix.

reasoning: Field reconciliation 2026-08-29 (see evidence tail). Vulnerability first: the advisory names the sink precisely — the per-call options parameter of java() reaching the JVM command line unvalidated, exploitable via Stanford wrappers with -agentpath/-javaagent/@argfile. Code archaeology pins the sink's birth to 5ac475d2ab95 (2026-07-04, #3683): it created the per-call parameter, spliced caller options directly into cmd, and converted the wrappers to use it — the exact unvalidated channel the advisory describes; the pre-existing global path was already guarded by 9e20c3eee792. BIC choice follows the named-sink rule (commit creating the advisory's named per-call options sink with missing validation). squash_decomposed=true: the flaw builds on the 9e20c3eee792 global-validation commit, which the per-call path silently bypassed. AI decision: BIC-only attribution — the BIC object carries only the human identity KKfine with no AI marker, so NOT_AI; the remediation-side Claude Sonnet 4.6 co-author trailer on 9e20c3eee792 (a different, earlier defect's fix) is recorded as evidence-only metadata.
